messages:
Maya: :rotating_light: Getting alerts that the ALB in us-west-2 is deregistering targets for /inference-edge target group (tg-0a1b2c3d). Started ~5m ago, lots of 503s from customers. Anyone oncall?

deploy-bot: [ALERT] ALB target_health_unhealthy: target group tg-0a1b2c3d — 12/12 targets Unhealthy. first_seen=1748000000

Ben: Can you paste the pod readiness state + logs? My first guess is readiness probe flapping or slow cold startups.

Maya: kubectl output attached: ```
NAME                                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
inference-edge-5f6d7c8d9b-abc12         0/1     Running   0          3m
inference-edge-5f6d7c8d9b-def34         1/1     Running   0          22m
```
Logs for the 0/1 pod show model load taking ~18s on startup and then readiness probe failing with timeout: 
```
[2026-03-05T21:12:34Z] INFO loading model shards...
[2026-03-05T21:12:52Z] WARN readiness probe timed out after 1s
```

Ben: That matches. Current readinessProbe in k8s is low: ```yaml
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 10
  timeoutSeconds: 1
  failureThreshold: 3
```
TimeoutSeconds=1 is too aggressive for cold-starting GPU-backed model loads.

Sanjeev: Two things: (1) increase readiness timeout and add startupProbe so K8s won't mark it unready during model load; (2) tune ALB target group health check to be more tolerant during rollouts. ALB defaults are interval=30s, timeout=5s, unhealthyThreshold=2 which can deregister quickly if k8s toggles readiness.

Carter: Also noticed this is concentrated in the edge nodes in ap-northeast-1 — our NAT gateway in that AZ had high SNAT exhaustion earlier, causing S3/model pulls to slow down. If model download is delayed, readiness will fail. We should check nat gw metrics.

Maya: Confirmed: NAT gw CloudWatch shows port exhaustion spike at 21:10. Some pods hit slower I/O. So root cause is a combination: cold-start + NAT contention + strict readiness/ALB settings.

Ben: Immediate mitigation: 1) bump readiness timeoutSeconds to 5 and initialDelaySeconds to 15; 2) add a startupProbe so the kubelet doesn't kill the pod: ```yaml
startupProbe:
  exec:
    command: ["/bin/grpc_health_probe", "-addr=:8080"]
  failureThreshold: 30
  periodSeconds: 10
```
Also annotate Ingress with a temporary slower deregistration: 
```yaml
alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/target-group-attributes: "deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds=60,slow_start.duration_seconds=30"
```
That should reduce churn while we fix the NAT/GW scaling.

Sanjeev: Agreed. For long-term: (a) scale NAT gateway (or use Egress ENIs) for edge AZs, (b) move large model pulls to pre-warmed initContainers or a local cache on node, (c) make ALB health checks hit a lightweight /live endpoint for liveness and keep readiness for readiness.

Carter: I'm on NAT scaling. Will open a ticket to add an additional NAT gateway in ap-northeast-1 AZ-b and update route tables. ETA ~30m.

Maya: I'll push a quick deployment with readiness/startupProbe + ALB annotation as a hotfix. Pushing PR now, rolling to 10% canary.

Ben: Thanks. Once canary looks good, increase canary to 50% then full. Monitor target group healthy count and ALB 5xx rates.

Maya: Canary succeeded. Targets stabilized, ALB shows 12/12 healthy again. Monitoring for 15 more mins. :thumbsup:

Carter: NAT scaling done. CloudWatch shows SNAT ports back to normal.

Maya: Closing for now. Action items: 1) follow-up PR to add startupProbe + safer defaults; 2) run a pre-warm cache experiment for model pulls; 3) track ALB target attr defaults in runbook. Created ticket INFRA-2247: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-2247

Ben: Add a note in the runbook to check NAT port exhaustion and to prefer startupProbe for GPU services.

Maya: Will do. Thanks everyone.
